items.title: Need Help as First Time Writer
items.text:
Need Help as First Time Writer
I'm currently in the process of writing my first novel and I can force myself to sit down and write. However, I'm no good at writing the story. I can't seem to narrow my view to that of a single POV for writing the actual narrative. When I write, I love writing "grand scheme" things such as history, lore, or world building. I just seem to have a problem bringing that love of writing to a single POV. I either doubt myself or can't think of where to start or where to go with the story. 

Does anyone have any advice that might help?
Do you have any suggestions for studying material? I've done some light research but sorting the good advice from the bad advice is hard when you are just starting out.
I've referenced some of my favorite writers before and it does seem to help. Thank you for showing me I'm on the right track there! I'll be sure to continue that practice.

Recently I've started to come to terms with that. I have to force myself away from the frame of thinking that suggests that my first book will be madly successful and will make me incredibly rich. :P

Also, thank you for reminding me that I should make mistakes. I've always believed that you learn more from your failures than you do your successes. I'll be sure to remember that while I'm writing.

>Writing is a discipline and it takes time to build just like anything else.

Thank you for the reminder! This is something that I try to keep fresh in my head.

>study dialogue and character building

I definitely think that that is one of my problems. I need to hone my focus as a reader to understand the smaller pieces of a story.

>Try writing the same scene from different POVs and see which you like best. 

This is an exercise that I've never tried but I've always thought might work. I will definitely try it!

>If you're writing in 3rd person, a single POV isn't necessary. In fact, writing in a 3rd person narrative invites (demands?) multi-POVs.

When I read this, something clicked in my head. All of a sudden I saw that my interest in looking at the world rather than one character could be used. I enjoy watching the pieces of a world come together and if I write 3rd person, I fell like that is exactly what will happen. Each piece (or character) will seem random at the beginning but then come together by the end of the story. 

My brain tells me, while writing, that a scene has to have a character that is the main focus. Now that I think of the basics of 3rd person, maybe that isn't true?

>Forget POV (imho)... and just write [...]

This struck a chord as well. I struggle with "shut up and write" frequently when the time comes. I need a giant sign above my computer that says, "Just write the damn book."

>So become your own protagonist and live whatever fantasy daydream that you're concocting.

I don't think I've heard this anywhere else but it seems to me that it's a fundamental part of writing that I forget about often. I have to remember that writing a novel is something I want to do, not something I have to do.

I read this right before I went to bed and my thoughts went wild. Long story short, my character doesn't have a problem. My world does. He has no personal connection to the problem and I think that might be part of the problem. I've tried very hard to write a three dimensional character. Honestly, I did. However, I think I forgot to care about my own writing enough to make my character important to the reader and the story.

items.title: Character Motivation Problem
items.text:
Character Motivation Problem
I struggle with character motivation. I just can't seem to get a character to CARE about what is happening in my narratives. I have interesting plot, I have developed characters, but I can't come up with a way to connect my character to the conflict without using The Chose One trope. I'll take help or a simple redirect to helpful content.


EDIT: Becuase this seems to be a common problem, I'm going to add plot information to this post.


Main Character: Sage/Idealist Philosopher/Lore keeper.

-He's a thinker, not a doer. Worried he can't do anything to help.

-He doesn't care about anything except his research.

-Reclusive and subconsciously depressed.

-Prefer to seek greater knowledge than to fight for self preservation.


Major Conflict: A Celestial Titan is escaping the void to destroy the world.


Major (possible) Resolution: An Earth Titan is summoned and the Celestial Titan is locked in the void.


Theme: natural (Earth Titan) versus supernatural (Celestial Titan).

I'll do my best to give a watered down example without having to post all of my planning. :P

&#x200B;

Main Character: Male Sage/Idealist Philosopher/Lore Keeper. His personal goal and core desire revolve around understanding why life exists and understanding the universe.

Major Conflict: Celestial titan escapes the void to kill the world.

Major (possible) Resolution: Summon earth titan as protector.

&#x200B;

The theme of the story is heavily mankind versus nature (noting this in case it helps).
I like the idea that you presented here. I definitely think it's worth looking at. I'm going to look into how this could work in the parameters of my story.
Thank you, I will look into it!

Both UnusDeo and you have said something that is correct and I figure I would elaborate to aid in your discussion.

UnusDeo said he's a philosopher. I agree and add that my main character is a thinker, not a doer. In his own words, "I'm only one person, how could I save the world?"

You said he doesn't care about anything and you are absolutely right. He doesn't care about anything. He's a hermit-like recluse with no close family or friends. The only thing he thinks is worth his time is his research. This, however, is wholly not by chose. It's more of a depression thing but don't tell him that. ;)
I have something like this already worked into my outline but the Fantastic Beasts reference has given me a solid example of it working so I thank you!
Thank you. :)

Thank you for pointing this out! I never noticed this but now that you mention it, I see it. Almost too clearly. I see that this titan conflict isn't as clear as I would want it to be or it doesn't fit in with my theme the way I intended it to. You seem to suggest a shift from "mankind vs. nature" to "supernatural vs. natural". I agree with this and it's really cleaned up my theme fairly well.

My intention was **mankind versus the celestial titan** (natural \[mankind\] versus supernatural \[celestial titan\], as you've suggested). Mankind wins with the aid of the earth titan. (More on this later in my post.) What you inferred was **mankind versus titans (plural)** (again, natural \[mankind\] versus supernatural \[titans\] but with that earth titan bit mixed up)? 

Now, I see that those two are pretty similar. I also see that there might be a confusion with the earth titan that may need some fixing. I want the earth titan to stand out as a representation of nature, or man and the celestial titan to stand out as supernatural.

I think a clarification of my theme results in **natural (Earth Titan) versus supernatural (Celestial Titan).** 

I know I haven't even scratched the surface of this but it's getting late so I will end this post here and just keep thinking about it.

Thank you so much for your help!

Throughout my research I have seen the Sage as a supportive role; that mentoring bit you've mentioned. Although, I usually love this archetype as that support character (Gandalf, Yoda, Dumbledore), I wanted to see if I could write a main character that was The Sage without making him a mentor. Maybe it's impossible, maybe not. I'm not fully committed to turning him into a support character just yet. This is an idea that would fit into my outline, though, so thank you!
I forgot to even mention the character motivation bit! I'll do that tomorrow.

That was one of the things I was worried about. I'm not above modifying the character to make it fit. I'm going to be thinking about this over the next few days.

He isn't a pacifist by any means, it's more of a burning doubt about his helpfulness. Hence the motivation issue. I'll see if I can add a character trait that relates to taking action when necessary and then make his involvement necessary. If that makes any sense.

You are being helpful! You're giving me things to think about that no one else has.

He cares about his research. It's probably the only thing he cares about. I'll use that as a hook for motivation and see what I can brainstorm.
That makes a lot of sense, thank you!

Update: I've come up with motivation in the form of the "inability to act" character trait. Something happened early in his life and he couldn't do anything. Now that he is the only one who knows how the world is ending, hes going to push past his insecurities and do what needs to be done.

This seems like the best route for me right now and I'm going to be working it into my outline over the next few days. Any more comments or helpful redirection are much appreciated.

Thank you to everyone who has helped!

That makes sense. I was wary of the Chosen One trope because I feel like it's been over done in the genre I'm aiming for and, being a first-time author, and more than likely a self-published author when the time comes, I don't to damage my chances by making any of my content cliche.
It has, thank you. I think you've brought up an interesting angle for the Chosen One trope that doesn't sound cliche. Chosen by the majority rather than a faceless, unnamed entity or destiny.

I'm currently working on my first novel but I've found a method that has worked well for me. 

The idea that I had was for a few main characters and scenes. I took the scenes and put them in an order or what happened; a simple timeline of the events. Then, I took the characters, wrote them down, and thought about who they were. That was just basic stuff like personality. 

After that I worked on stretching out my timeline, much like the Snowflake Method of writing. I added, mostly, events but sometimes I would add background information, like mythology/history, or basic character stuff.

By this time I had a main character that I thought worked for the story. I took that main character and dove into fleshing it out; from personality to motivations.

Then, it's just basically expanding on everything I have.

&#x200B;

During the whole process I wrote down any further ideas that came to me while driving, eating, showering, etc.
